comments.author: Acid_Viking
comments.body:
There are too many tells that this is AI video for it to be serviceable as a game trailer. There are big ones, like the ogre head, but also many small details that will register to the viewer as something being off. For example, around 2:20, he has her impaled, but there's no sense of weight on the staff. It feels like she's hovering, and while she's hovering, he jabs with the staff, but her body doesn't move with it. There's also not a massive wound in her belly at 2:46. If you aren't able to achieve polished, professional results, the main effect of your trailer will be to advertise your use of AI.

I personally don't care for cinematic trailers, as they tell me nothing about the game. I'd rather see gameplay. A less ambitious trailer would probably be more effective.

Last but not least, never put a character in bikini armor.

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
sup, animator here, ill just say this. less is more man.  the longer your AI stuff is the more issues will appear.  You can cut in reall close in fight scenes, it helps sell the impact of action and it helps avoid unfortunate editing.  there are a couple of scenes you have cut in the middle to add an extra clip to extend it. in these situations its better to just cut to a different angle and make it more snappy.   
just my opinion. plus the gratuitous 'breast shot' was pretty lame.
